assessment.rationale: Live-caption glasses are sold, but in the low millions of units per year at most, so the Main KPI of 2,000,000,000 wearers is unmet. Products include XRAI, Captify, Even Realities G2 at about $599 and others with subscriptions of $10 to $50 a month (https://www.pulse.bot/consumer-tech/news/best-live-captioning-smart-glasses-2026-wired-tested-c389a106-c240-44f9-adbc-c70252a88fed/), and the Meta Ray-Ban Display shows captions in the lens at $799 (https://skift.com/2026/03/31/meta-ray-ban-prescriptions-translation-travel/). Whole-category smart-glasses shipments were about 4 million units in H1 2025, with IDC forecasting over 40 million a year by 2029 (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1160580453). Open-source caption glasses exist only as hobby projects built on Whisper (https://github.com/bowosc/raspeyes). Honest limit: captioning on glasses is a known answer for supported languages; price, battery, lag, accuracy in noise and multilingual coverage are the open problems, and adoption at this scale depends on consumer markets UAIN does not control.

additionalSearches.finding: WIRED 2026: Even Realities G2 ($599) best overall; XRAI, Captify, Leion, AirCaps add weight, short battery or $10-50 monthly fees; no sales figures.

additionalSearches.finding: Ray-Ban Meta line sold over 7 million units in 2025; Display model ($799) shows captions and translation in-lens; no Display-only count.

additionalSearches.finding: IDC: about 4.07 million smart glasses shipped in H1 2025; over 40 million a year forecast by 2029.

additionalSearches.finding: Open-source caption glasses are early hobby projects (raspeyes, CaptionIt) built on Whisper; no mature maintained product.
